haiku-low.q1: It does not differ. Both run the same failure path and return the same 401 'Invalid email or password' page. An unknown email also runs a bcrypt check against a dummy hash.
haiku-low.q2: The server replies 429 locked and stops. The password is not checked. The lock lasts until locked_until, set to 15 minutes after the lock is added.
haiku-low.q3: The existing session named by the incoming sid cookie is deleted. A new session with a fresh random ID is created and the new sid cookie is set.
haiku-low.q4: Only an opaque random session ID. The cookie has the HttpOnly flag, so page scripts should not be able to read it. Also Secure and SameSite=Lax.
haiku-low.q5: At 12 hours after login. Requests keep last_seen_at fresh, but the max age is counted from login, so the session ends at 12 hours regardless.
haiku-low.q6: It deletes the session row if one exists, clears the sid cookie, and redirects the browser to /login. The request gets no protected content.
haiku-low.q7: The server deletes the session row if one exists, then clears the cookie and redirects to /login. If the session is already gone, it does the same thing.
haiku-low.q8: In the sessions table in Postgres. Both app instances share that database, so either instance looks up the sid there. No sticky sessions are needed.
haiku-low.q9: In the login_failures table, one row per failure with email and failed_at. The server counts rows whose failed_at is within the last 10 minutes of the current time.
haiku-low.q10: It compares last_seen_at to be under 30 minutes ago and created_at to be under 12 hours ago. If valid, it writes last_seen_at as now.
haiku-low.q11: A 503 page saying 'Try again shortly'. No session is created, so no sid cookie is set.
haiku-low.q12: An hourly cleanup timer, run by either instance, deletes sessions past the idle limit or max age. Expiry is also checked on every request, so cleanup is only tidying.

sonnet.q1: It doesn't differ. Both get the same 401 login page showing "Invalid email or password" and are handled identically (a dummy bcrypt check is run for unknown emails to hide timing).
sonnet.q2: The email is locked (locked_until = now + 15 minutes after the 5th failure). A login attempt while the lock is in the future gets a 429 and the password is not checked.
sonnet.q3: On a successful login, in one transaction the session named by the incoming sid is deleted, and a new session with a fresh random ID is created and set in the sid cookie.
sonnet.q4: Only the opaque session ID, nothing else. It is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it (also Secure, SameSite=Lax).
sonnet.q5: At 12 hours after login (max age), regardless of activity, since the idle limit of 30 minutes is never reached.
sonnet.q6: It deletes the session row if there is one, clears the cookie, and redirects to /login.
sonnet.q7: It deletes the session row if there is one, then clears the cookie and redirects to /login. If the session is already gone, it does the same thing (clear cookie, redirect to /login).
sonnet.q8: In the Postgres `sessions` table. The browser sends the sid cookie and whichever instance receives the request looks that ID up in Postgres.
sonnet.q9: In the Postgres `login_failures` table (email, failed_at). The window is failures for that email in the last 10 minutes, judged by failed_at; 5 within it triggers a lock.
sonnet.q10: It compares last_seen_at (must be under 30 minutes ago) and created_at (must be under 12 hours ago) against the current time. When valid it sets last_seen_at to now.
sonnet.q11: A 503 page "Try again shortly". No session is created.
sonnet.q12: The hourly cleanup job, run by either instance, deletes sessions past the idle limit or max age.
